lines.line: Hmm... Hello?
Is the connection working?
Alright. I'm not used to recording my voice like this. It's Mira. Mira Kalinina. Do you... know about me? That's great if you do.

Have you heard... that voice? It might sound strange, but... I often hear it in my head. Especially when I'm trying to fall asleep. When I'm trying to turn off my brain, to not think about anything. Like...
My head is like a room full of shelves, filled with different books where I write my thoughts. Everything is interconnected, and everything has its cause and effect.

But right now, there's a scraping noise, an unsettling knock breaking through the door, growing louder and louder, like a police squad trying to cut through my cozy apartment door, ready to throw all my things around, break everything, and make a mess.

I can't hear my own thoughts; it's like they're muffled by thick cotton. I start to feel scared, and anxiety starts to pinch my nerves. Gradually, from this noise, words begin to form. Words asking for help. Someone is calling out to me in pain.

Their being is about to shatter from unbearable pain. Just a little more, and it feels like something terrible will happen. The knocking beats an erratic rhythm, joined by the sharp sounds of a synthesizer...

// my_material.silicon heart beats. #SET BITS = CONSENT sirens->city, where 
for each(pixel, blood){ - each drop of blood, each byte - a soul's scream == exception.logging() }
// Fated to be forever trapped in the web of one's own algorithms, imprisoned in the spider's web of the meat machine
So, is it recording? Valya, get out of the shot.
Stop, Zhenya, move to the left, grab that bunny.
Not my left... Jesus Christ...
Now this... Move to the right.
Don't just stand there like a log, damn it!
Mira, what was next for you? Come on, quickly, Sanych, are you filming?
-She woke me up... Like with cold water or something like that.
-Zhenya, did you hear?
The icy splash immediately brought me to my senses. My head was buzzing, and a nauseating lump rose in my throat.
A ringing in my ears stunned me, and for a few seconds, the music stopped.
-Mira, are you okay? Are you alright? Mira? I'm sorry, I didn't know it would be like this, really, I didn't know. Chick told me that nothing would happen from two grams, but... did you get hurt?
Sonya is rambling, and I can barely make out the words. Oh fuck, why do I feel so awful... The ringing in my ears won't stop. I'm about to pass out again...
-Sonya, get lost!
I barely managed to push her away, so the stream of vomit wouldn't splatter on her clothes.
-Oh!
She stepped back in surprise.
-So that... I'll ever... listen to you again...
-I promise, it won't happen again... Really!
-Sonya... You're an idiot.
There are people all around, but it's like they don't notice me. Which is just as well; I don't look great. After throwing up, I feel a bit better.
-Would you stop being mad if I, for example... If I gave you something?
-Like what? A half-smoked cigarette? You're always taking mine... But sure, you can try!
It seems like she took my words seriously.
Honestly, I can't stay mad at her. I look at that silly face, even now, and I feel happy.
I don't know why. In any case, no one can get through the polar night alone. But with Sonya, there's never a dull moment.
Sonya is thinking about something. Looks like she's planning something again.
-Hey, let's... keep partying!
-I'm not in the mood...
-Come on! The night's only just begun!
-Good one...
I haven't danced in so long. And now, right after I just threw up...

Sonya grabbed my hand, pulled me off the floor, and led me to the center of the dance floor, pushing through the crowd. I barely had any strength left, so I had to follow her lead. I have this strange feeling of deja vu...
And sometimes I forget that it happened...
The smell of her clothes... Will it ever fade?
-Hey, why are you just standing there? Coming?
I closed my eyes.
Sonya moved with such fluidity, like she didn't have a single bone in her body, following the rhythm, spreading her arms from time to time to trace cosmic shapes.
I just followed her, trying to repeat her moves. Everyone around started yelling - the "madness" had started.
Sonya threw her arms up, becoming one with the music, like a sound wave in harmony.
Every note resonated through her body and thin legs.
I immediately fell behind and stopped. Had she practiced this dance at home? Oh right, she ordered this track. So unfair! I've had enough...
I'll go, take a breather.
-Mira?
-I need the bathroom.
I pushed my way to the bathroom and locked myself in a filthy stall. My hands went up to pinch my nose to keep the acidic smell from burning my lungs.
-God, my eyes sting...
-What's this?
An injector, a new one. Familiar label "SPAM," but the color is different. And there's a number 2. All the other injectors didn't have a number. What does that mean?
This will help me concentrate.
I've had enough.
A ringing in my ears. That voice. It's coming back.
I threw up right where a human hand was sticking out. Tearing the door off its hinges, I bolted outside, fell to the floor, then slipped on the tiles and fell again on the wet tiles.
I threw up right where a human hand was sticking out. Tearing the door off its hinges, I bolted outside, fell to the floor, then slipped on the tiles and fell again on the wet tiles.
-Holy crap!
Sonya was blocking the bathroom entrance. I knocked her over and ran for the club exit. It was dark outside - time to get used to it. The cold air hit me like a wave of fresh chill to the face.
Alright, alright... Nothing is alright!
What should I do?!
Run, run, run far away from this messed up place!
I looked at my hands, blackened from that rotten slime. If this washes off, it'll be with my skin.
There were so many people there... And what if they talk about me? That's it!
My weakened legs carried me as best they could toward the tram stop.
I stopped, momentum carrying me a bit farther, almost tripping over the curb. I looked around. Sonya was nowhere in sight.
Maybe I shouldn't have run... Maybe I drew even more attention to myself that way. And my throat hurts... I spat on the pavement, trying to get rid of the taste of blood.
Sonya definitely won't believe that I killed someone and stuffed them into a toilet. But... How do I prove it to the police? Maybe I should pray that they don't come after me?
Why does weird stuff always happen to me? It feels like something cracked a couple of days ago, and through that crack, more and more misfortunes are creeping into my life. I hope it's not forever.
In these thoughts, I didn't notice my tram arriving. As usual, there's no one here at night. Who are these trams even for? Can't be just for me...
-It's your fault. It's all because of you! I'll keep reminding you of this until you finally feel ashamed, until you repent!
-Mira, come on, there's nothing you can do now, you should probably just... accept it.
-Well, I won't accept it. I can't stand to look at you! You slut!
My teeth gritted on their own, causing a dull ache.
-Come on, it'll be fun, I promise! I've done it a hundred times. There's nothing cooler than an acid rave!
-Alright, get ready for it. A-and three!
I still haven't gotten over it. My thoughts are all jumbled, reality and memories blending together. When Sonya injected me with that stuff, I felt something... strange.
Some unusual connection between me and everyone around. Not something ordinary, like friendly feelings, but something mystical, that I can't explain. Now this feeling is slowly fading.
SPAM-2. Could the effect of this stuff be even stronger? Honestly, I have no desire to turn myself inside out again.
Through a sleepy haze, I heard a rasping voice say "Aeshaphot" Damn, almost missed my stop.
The noisy doors opened, creaking on their hinges, and I crawled to my doorstep.
One last effort to climb the stairs, and I can finally rest and think things over. The heavy metal door clanged shut, and I climbed to my floor.
Each step is hard, the weakness in my legs and dizziness won't let go. The last flight of stairs. I looked up, and there in front of me was a huge box.
Is this... Sonya's gift? She got a taxi that fast?
Despite the exhaustion, I dragged the box inside the apartment, holding onto the massive lid.
-Fuck!
The lid flew off, and my butt hit the floor with a thud.
On the caught lid, there's a tag.
"To Sonychu <3." No doubt. It's from her. The handwriting is unusually beautiful and neat. I look down at the box's contents, and my heart stops. It's...
Standing before me is the latest Hexa-98 computer model. I screamed with overwhelming emotions.
Sonya... You're just... You're just...
I love you, Sonya!
I instantly pulled the heavy machine out of the box. The glossy buttons on the keyboard gleamed in the light, like white chocolate.
The color screen, the system unit packed with mezzanine boards, the built-in modem... I'll finally be able to connect to the Net!
I could never have dreamed that here, now, I would have such power. From tech classes, I know a bit about this system.
All I need to do is go into the modem settings and connect to the Net... The operator's page loaded in just a couple of minutes.
With trembling hands, I entered the code from the card.
"Welcome to Lisnet, Mira."
I melted into my chair, overwhelmed by emotion.
-What was that "ping"? Seems like I got a message, but how?
I closed the browser and clicked on the Courier icon. It turns out it's already registered in my name.
New message.
Hello, Mira. So, you've finally made it online. I've been waiting for this. We'll meet soon. Kir.
It seems there's a stranger in the Net. I can reply to him.
I don't know you. Who are you?
If you want, I can walk you to school. We could meet outside your place.
He knows my name and address... Maybe it's some classmate trying to mess with me? What if it's not?
Ok. But I'm always late ;)
-Mira, you're online!
-I guess I am?
-And you said you didn't need any of this!
-Well... it just happened :)
Hugging my knees, I watch the digital clock in the corner of the screen. Time is relentlessly approaching eight. Looks like I won't be able to rest.
Oh well, to hell with it. I'll try not to think about anything, plus there are still a couple of hours left. I open the page list. So many different links, I don't even know where to start.
Fluffy Delights? What?
The loading page reveals picture after picture, full of kittens of all shapes and sizes, fluffy and sleek, and even totally hairless.
What??? They really come like that? And why are they on "FLUFFY Delights"?
There are so many pages... You could spend a lifetime here!
Suddenly, some of the kittens start moving - dancing, jumping, and surrounded by sparks and flowers.
Whoa! In the Net, pictures come to life!
A six-eyed cat stares at me. Not like the other pictures, but right into my soul...
-What are you looking at?

The cat blinked all six of its eyes.
Creepy to see it here. I wonder if it's a drawing or a photo montage?
It looks like it's about to jump.
Meow!
Breaking through the screen, the enormous six-eyed cat flies straight at me, digging its claws into my face.
What? The alarm? Was I asleep?
It's five to nine; I'm going to be late! The stranger in Courier is still online. Just as I thought, it was someone's bad joke.
Pulling the plug from the machine, I quickly put on my shoes and stomped down the stairs.
No one was waiting for me downstairs. Weird...
Maybe "Kir" got tired of waiting. An impatient stranger... Probably for the best.
Bag over my shoulder - let's go. Honestly, this eternal darkness is driving me crazy, even though the polar night only started a couple of days ago.
It feels like the city is frozen in one moment, savoring it, savoring this gloom and cold lonely night bit by bit.
If you silence your inner voice, your head fills with the hum of wires and transformers, which is hard to shake.
Thinking with that noise is torture. So, I try to constantly talk to myself about something. Like now - about how important it is to talk to myself. Funny...
Someone's hand landed on my shoulder. I jumped back a bit in fright and turned around.
-Hey, what the hell? Who are you?
Maybe it's that stranger? Honestly, he looks kind of strange.
-Sorry for scaring you. I'm Kir. I sent you that message.
-How did you even know my address? And my Net profile?
I looked him over from head to toe for the first time.
-I've never seen you before.
-I... just moved here recently. This week. They accepted me at your school, so I... decided to meet you.
-I'm used to people only leaving this city - as far away as possible. What could you have found here?
-The romance of endless nights and city lights, the smell of damp grass... All of it makes coming here worthwhile.
-Oh really?
-Just kidding. Come on, we're already late.
-I feel like you're hiding something.
Kir looked away and sighed.
-Maybe I am. Why do you care?
-I just... want to know more about you.
-Sometimes it's better to know nothing than to know the truth.
-Quit being so mysterious; just tell me.
-A pencil.
-I stabbed a pencil into my desk partner's eye.
-The principal wanted to cover it up, so... now I'm here.
-Are you serious?
-Absolutely.
-And... why?
Kir shrugged casually. An awkward silence hung between us.
I trudged along behind Kir. Wires connecting the modules of some strange electronic contraption swung back and forth in time with his steps.
-Hey, sorry for asking, but... what's that thing?
-What thing?
I felt embarrassed by my own question. Even though technology is evolving quickly, that's no excuse to fall behind.
-Oh, you mean the electronics... This is a portable 'Moby.' Thirty-two megabytes of RAM, two parallel processing units.
-No way... In such a small box...
-It's tied to my... hobbies. I don't know how I'd live without my 'Moby.'

So many secrets... Fine, keep them. 
We walked on a carpet of shadows, trying not to trip over random rocks or branches.
-Hey, do you have a flashlight by any chance?
-Nope. Actually, I'd advise against using one.
-Why's that?
-With a flashlight, you only see what it points at. But if your eyes adjust to the darkness, you'll see much more.
Kir rubbed his eyes.
-Are you local?
-Yeah. I was born here. Never, ever left.
-Then you must know where those lanterns come from.
-It's a festival marking the start of the polar night. It'll last almost half a year, and people release lanterns that look like bright yellow suns.
-If you want, we can go to the festival sometime... later. I bet half the class ran off to it... Must be fun right now.
-Why can't we go now?
-School. You ask so many questions, it might actually do you some good.
-I already know this year's program.
-No kidding.
-For real.
-Then why are you going?
-Well... I'm walking you. Maybe I can help with something. You can tell me about the city, and I'll help you with math.
-No thanks, I can handle it myself.
-Suit yourself, just thought I'd offer.
-Smooth talker, meow.
-Huh, what?
-Did you say something?
-No... no, nothing. You know, I'm not feeling great. You go on; I'll stay here. Need to pull myself together.
-Need help?
-No, thanks. Go on.
I looked back and saw a huge pink cat with six eyes. I froze in shock.
-You're staring like you've never seen a talking cat. And really, that's fucking rude.
What did I just say? What's going on?
-Are you... real?
-As real as it gets. I'll be sticking around now. Reach out if you need anything.
-But I don't need a cat, I mean... well, where will you even live?
-In your apartment, meow.
-I have no idea how to take care of a cat, and anyway... I have to go to school now, so... bye. I gotta go.
The cat just stood there, stunned, and I backed away toward the school.

I shook my head side to side. What the hell is going on? First a corpse in the toilet, now this. What is happening? Maybe I'm dreaming... I pinched my arm. No, I'm not asleep. I must just be really, really tired. I need some sleep.
The school building was dead quiet. I quickly found the right classroom. I could hear the teacher's voice through the wall.
-Now joining the class is Kir - he's moved here from afar. Be kind to him and help him adjust to our school life.
I entered, apologizing to the teacher for being late. Waiting for me in the classroom were Kir, Sonya, and Alina. There were empty seats next to each of them. Understandably.
Who should I sit next to?

I feel bad for Alina; she's always alone... And I'm still curious about this new kid in class... But I always sit with Sonya. I think she'll be upset if I sit with someone else. Even if it's just for one class.
-Hey! I nudge Sonya's shoulder and plop down at the desk. If I don't do this greeting ritual first, she'll get me later.
-Ow! I didn't notice you. We have a new kid, can you believe it? I'm shocked, someone actually showed up in our backwater; that never happens! They only transferred people from other classes...
-Quiet, everyone! Yefifanov, glue that butt to the chair! Today's lesson... Ugh, what's the deal!
-Yeah, I know.
Sonya looked at me questioningly over her glasses.
-Wait, what do you mean...
-Yeah, we already met. He walked me to school...
-No way! You're kidding!
-Back row!!!
We went quiet and started talking in hushed tones.
He actually walked you?
-Yeah. What's the big deal? I'm not that interested...
-Well, I don't know...
Sonya leaned back in her chair.
-People are connected, no matter how far apart they are. What did I say that's so funny?
-He walked you specifically, so that's something.
-Are you... jealous or something?
-No-no! You're imagining things. I don't like him at all, and...
Sonya noticeably blushed.
-One more warning, and you're both out of this classroom!
-Ugh, we're talking quietly. What's his problem?
-How did you two even... I mean... meet? He didn't just randomly come by your place?
-We met online. Actually, he messaged... on Courier.
-How'd he get your nickname? How did he even find it?
I raised my hands in sincere confusion.
-I have no idea. And... I wanted to ask you, you know a lot about the Net... Is it possible to find out somehow... indirectly?
-In theory... If you'd entered your nickname on some page, he could've stolen it... But it's impossible since he messaged you right as you got online.
That means he couldn't have learned your nickname from classmates.
-Using the fourth network protocol, we can chat, exchange photos...
-Did you tell him?
-Me? I've never even seen him before! And I'm never talking to him again!
Sonya blushed again.
-Mira, out into the hallway.
Sonya and I groaned in unison, "Ughhhh."
-Why does she always kick you out?
I trudged to the door.
The old bell rang, signaling the end of the lesson, and the classroom emptied instantly.
Some people ran off for a snack, others to smoke in the back courtyard. I couldn't believe my eyes - where Kir had been sitting, there was a SPAM injector.
Could it be... He's using it too?
I had to quickly grab and hide it before anyone noticed.

I'm going crazy. I'm definitely going crazy. This past week has been nothing but madness. I just want to forget everything. Forget the smell of the rotting corpse, that nasty cat, and be normal. I've had enough.
Curiosity overpowered my fear of the unknown, and I took out the injector. Maybe this will help me feel better? I drove the needle into my leg.

-Did I... pass out? I...
These letters... Numbers... Too many... I can't...
Grasp a single thought...

It feels like I've left my body... and I'm controlling it from outside... It's so light, but...
I can't control myself at all.
So fast...
-Who's that? Kir? Are you here?
-Do this. Make a 'V' with your fingers. Focus.

I managed to bend my hand into the right sign and hold it to my face. Focus? 
I tried to look through the narrow frame of my fingers.

The world around me begins to take shape, and instead of blurry spots, I see the city.
But... it's as if threads stretch out around me... intertwining everything.
I looked at Kir. His whole body was one big green spot of threads.
W-what is this?
-These are connections. See?
A thin green thread extended between me and Kir. I touched it with my finger, and it trembled easily.
-Connections?
I unfocused my eyes, and the world blurred again into shapeless images, words, and numbers.
-Everything is connected. One way or another...
I looked at my body. Weak threads extended from it in different directions, even up to the sky and down into the earth. Is this real? Am I not imagining it, and all these connections really exist?
-What even are... these connections...
-I think you'll figure it out yourself in the 'Streams.' I have to go... We'll meet again.
It seems like the effects are wearing off. This injection works much less...
I feel sick. I'm going to...
Before I could even stand up, I threw up painfully, some slime hitting my shirt.
-I can't take this anymore...
-Mira, there you are! I've been looking all over for you! Are you sick? Mira? What happened?! I'll get a doctor!
-No, please... Just help me get to the bathroom.
Sonya helped me stand.
-What happened to you? It's because of me, right?
-Yeah, probably because of that injection.
-I didn't know it'd affect you like this... Well... I'm sorry... Remember... The gift... I...
I remembered the Hexa she gave me, and despite the weakness, I wrapped my arms around Sonya's neck, hugging her as tightly as I could.
-Thank you. You're the best!
-You need to wash up, come on, quickly. It'd be bad if anyone saw us like this. I feel like classmates will start whispering behind your back...
-No matter... Just take me there.
Sonya dragged me to the bathroom.
-What, feeling crappy?
That silly cat followed me again.
-What do you care...
-Seems like you're starting to like this whole drug thing. Just lying there, catching the spins, mind free from all this mess. Meow, that's the life.
-Well, well, don't get mad, seriously, I get it.
Sonya got me to the school bathroom.
-Need help? I can hold your hair or...
-No, I'm fine. Go back to class.
I went into the stall and locked the door.
The cat slid under the wooden door and stared at me.
-Are you just going to watch me?
He nodded affirmatively.
-I'm a cat, dammit. All cats do that.
Oh, why is this happening to me.
I plopped down on the toilet seat and felt something wet.
-Ahhh!
-Mira? You okay?
-Alright, I'll just have a smoke out here while you're busy.

I knew there was some kind of cult. I wonder why I've never heard of it before? And what's it called?
The Cult of the Fecal Angels?
So many questions...
-Sonya, look, do you see that?
-See what?
-The puddle, and that graffiti...
-And?
-I'm sure it's some kind of mystical ritual. Like, wax dripping from candles or something.
-Haha... Maybe! I think I know what you're getting at.
I shrugged.
-And what would that be?
-You want us to find the cultists in our school! And... join them!
-Whaaat...
-Or... turn them in to the police...
-No way am I turning them over to the cops.
-Actually, I think I know who did this. Let's go.
Sonya led me somewhere in the school basement, down a dark hallway.
In elementary school, we were never allowed down there - I just got in the habit of avoiding it.
Only one door in the concrete tunnel was open, and a light was shining through.
-This is your stop. She's weird, if you ask me. But... you wanted to meet her.
I stepped into a blindingly white room.
-Uh... hi?
I was instantly at a loss.
-Welcome to the Church of the Twenty-Eight Days. I can't see you, but... I can hear the tremble in your voice.
Her words wrapped around me like a soft blanket, making me feel an unusual comfort and calm, a kind of acceptance of the inevitable.
-Are you... an Angel?
-You may call me that. What brings you here?
-Signs... In the school bathroom. I saw an angel, and...
-Do you seek to learn our teachings?
-Yes! That's why I came.
-Good. Sit down.
The girl felt my face with her hands - with her blindfold, she couldn't see anything.
-Our commandments are simple. If something stands in your way to knowing God's truth, remove it.
-If what you see disturbs you... cut out your eyes... If your legs lead you away from God - cut them off.
I glanced at the rusty butcher knife lying casually next to me.
-God?
-Yes. Our one and only God.
Something inside me wanted to trust this girl.
-And if... If I have superpowers, does that mean I'm against God?
-Yes. Man shouldn't be able to do what only He is permitted to do.
-I... I see connections between everything around me... Like green threads linking all living things... All I need to do is place my fingers in a 'V' shape over my eyes.
-Then you should get rid of them.
-Cut... off my fingers?
-Yes. They bring you closer to God, but your purpose is to be on Earth, among people.

-Even if you're the best in the world - remain human.
Let this be your initiation.
-Alright. Let it be so.
I took the rusty butcher knife, raised my hand, and with all my strength, struck my finger lying on the table. A piece of flesh flew under the table, and blood started gushing from my finger.
-Ow... Why... How stupid of me...
The girl ripped the blindfold off her face, eyes wide in disbelief as she looked at me.
-You... You're nuts? It was supposed to be pretend...
Wrapping my finger in rags, we tried to find the missing piece, but it was no use.
Everyone rushed into the room and stared at me and the stream of blood from my finger.
It was hard to explain why I did it. It was like someone higher than me chose the dumbest option from two possible answers.
What if... if I can no longer see the connections? What if someone really is controlling me... Well, good luck with that.
When I got back to class from the nurse's office, everyone was shocked by what I did. Looks like the club is going to get shut down. And I'll be missing a finger... forever.
No way, my body is worth more to me than that.
-Sorry... You're nice, but I don't want to lose my fingers.
-Suit yourself... Then I can't initiate you.
The Angel shrugged.
If you change your mind, you know where to find us. You're always welcome here.
I left with a strange feeling.
Those damn jerk girls got into our bathroom and splattered everything with their disgusting dicks!
-Those disgusting perverts broke into our bathroom and covered everything with their gross dicks!
-What? W-wait... What are you talking about?!
-The puddle of semen, of course!
-How did you know it was... Never mind, I don't want to know...
-Doesn't matter! We need to find those creeps in our school.
-Fine... But how? You're gonna check under everyone's skirt?
-Hmm...
I thought about it seriously. Yeah, how would I even go about finding them...
-Well, it's simple - they'd be ugly, dressed poorly, and acting weird.
Walking out of the bathroom, we immediately bumped into some girls in the hallway. They were chatting about something, warming themselves by the windowsill.
We almost never talk to them, and when we do, it's only about school stuff. Perfect candidates for a beating.
-What do you want?
The chubby one turned to look at me with a scowl.
-I... I just wanted to ask something.
The girl on the right glanced at me with interest.
-There's a tranny at our school.
-Do I look like a guy?
-No... Do you play videogames?
-For a computer?
-Yeah.
-I don't play games.
-Well... I love Tamagotchis. And she's playing Dune. What kind of quiz is it anyway?
Hmm... Who of them is guilty?
It's definitely her. One hundred percent.
-Here, take this!
-Ouch! Are you crazy?
Holy shit, I think I was wrong. Let's run!
I bolted out of the corridor like a bullet, leaving the girls behind.
It seems my iron logic has failed somewhere.
-You got caught!
-What? How am I involved in this?
-Do you even know her?
-We just met today.
No doubt about it. I'm on the trail of the criminal.
-You'll learn your lesson for dressing like a girl and jerking off in our toilet!
The first blow between the legs knocked him to the ground. I pounced and started beating him with my fists.
-Hey, easy there, you'll kill him!
I was barely pulled away from the guy, depriving me of the opportunity to get revenge.
-Mira, how did you... How did you understand all this? How did you guess?
I shrugged nonchalantly.
-Probably a talent.
-Well, do you feel better?
-Sort of...
-Let's be honest. You chose the victim at random.
-Leave me alone...
-Now we're definitely going to have problems on exams. I think I've completely pissed off the teacher. And you too.
-I still don't give a shit.
-What are we going to do now... Maybe apologize? Maybe... I don't know!
-Well, since we're not going to class anymore, we can go for a walk.
-Where? To your place? To the festival? To the tower? Shopping? To the park? I want to go to the park! Mira, let's go to the park, okay?
-Okay, okay. Just leave me alone.
We just met Sonya, and I already have a headache.
-Amazing, fuck school! Screw it!
-Shush!
-What? What's wrong?
Sonya turned around looking for the cat.
-Forget it. Maybe I'll tell you later.

-So, see you soon?

Hell, this thing is heavy! For some reason, I tapped the metallic sphere and held it up to my ear. There was a hum inside. And this thing is supposed to connect to the Net? How will I look at the monitor? I don't understand how this even works.

I'm home.
Great! Put on the helmet and press the button on the right.
-Directly... on my head? But it'll cover my eyes... 0_o

I lifted the metallic sphere off the floor. My hands were shaking, and the shaking spread through my whole body... With effort, I shoved my head into the sphere. My head suddenly felt twice as heavy, and I rested it on the table.
It's dark... Absolutely pitch black. I feel around and find a button. Seems right. I'll press it.
Click - and nothing happens. Darkness surrounds me everywhere, no matter where I look.
Did I do something wrong? And what was even supposed to happen? I'm scared. Darkness is everywhere. I can't see my hands, my legs...
Somewhere in the back of my head, capacitors start to crackle. Did the sphere turn on? The electric hum fills my ears. It fills all the space in my head and pushes out all thoughts.
So scary...
So scary... A flash of white light. I screamed from the surprise.
... Mi... Mira? Can you hear me?

Breathe... just breathe.

-'Psyche' transmits brain impulses using the capabilities of the Network's fourth protocol.
-And everything around...
-Yes, our surroundings and bodies are generated by the brain. The brain uses memories of places and objects to create the image.
-Amazing, isn't it?
Kir spread his arms, showing off the technology's grandeur.
I touched his clothes. They felt... real.
-No, this can't be. I must be dead, or it's a dream. This is impossible... This can't be real...
-Step back!
I shoved Kir aside and bolted towards the classroom door.
There was a dance floor with a crowd of people dancing to some chaotic mix of sounds.
They didn't notice me kneeling in the middle of the hall.
-What...
-Why am I here?
I turned around. The door was gone.
-These are artifacts. Errors created by the brain during the simulation process. It happens... sometimes. When you're stressed out, or something like that.
-Did I... create this club here? But why?
-Maybe this place bothers you in some way.
-Maybe...
-You know, I... I didn't expect you'd react like this.
-How else was I supposed to react? I don't understand what's happening... I don't understand how I ended up here!

Kir froze, trying to find a way out of the situation.
-Maybe you'll feel better and calm down if... if I play something for you?
-You'll play?
Kir climbed onto the stage and picked up a guitar.
Wow, does he really play guitar? That's awesome!
He fiddled with some controls, switching cables from one socket to another.
A whole chain of little boxes with buttons was laid out across the stage, all connected by cables. A wire from the last box was plugged into the electric guitar.
The first strum spread like mist over the tiny hall.
My heart began to race in anticipation.
-Ahem... So, this song is for Mira Kalinina...
Somewhere in the background, as if from nowhere, drums started playing.
I feel... so strange... Like I'm in a dream! Like none of this is really happening to me...
Music flowed from the speakers. I'm not well-versed in genres, but I think this is called... post-punk? Though with all the effects, it sounded more like some kind of shoegaze.
Damn, I've never been to a concert before... Well, except for those embarrassing school performances.

I don't know what language he's singing in, but it sounds really good... Maybe I shouldn't treat him with so much... suspicion... If only Sonya were here to hear this... When I tell her, she'll be so jealous!
White smoke began to pour out from under the stage, covering everything up to my knees, turning the stage into a foggy hill.
Kir... Who are you really...
Cheers came from all around, and Kir took a bow to the invisible audience, then unstrapped his guitar and threw it onto the wooden floor.
-Hey, Kir, will you teach me?
-Do you want a mini-game, like in the original game?
-What?
-No, never mind...
-So, will you teach me?
-Why are you pestering me?
Kir laughed.
-Did you actually like it?
-Wow... Honestly, I've never played for a live audience before.
-You really should have.
-Do you think others would like it too?
-I'm sure you'd find someone to play for.
-Well... Now I can play for you, right?
I nodded.
-Yes. Of course, you can. Maybe we could organize a big concert at school?
-Thank you, Mira, I...
Kir froze, his mouth open in excitement.
-Hey?
-Everything okay?
-Kir?
I waved my hand in front of his glassy eyes. No response.
What a fuck is going on...
I walked around him, but couldn't find anything that resembled a door. Absolute silence surrounded me... Even thinking felt... annoyingly loud.
-Hey, is anyone here?
-Help!
I tried to push away the thought that I was stuck in this illusory world and that there was no way out, but... My heart was beating like a drunken drum, and my mind felt like thick jelly.
I'm scared...
So scared...
-Kir, please, say something! Please!
I hit the frozen mannequin with all my strength. Nothing happened.
-Let me out! Let me out! Let me out!
Three... Two... One! At the count of one, I dashed towards the wall to smash into it with my head, but at the last moment, I veered off.
No... I have to try again.
Three... Two... One!
This time, I hit the club wall straight on. No... Nothing...
It's not working.
I slumped down against the wall and closed my eyes.
How long have I been sitting here?
An hour?
A day?
A week?
Time has stopped.
I opened my eyes. Darkness...
Endless darkness.
Maybe I'll stay here forever?
Wait...
Darkness...
I reached out and took off the metallic sphere from my head.
What? Only a couple of minutes have passed?
Maybe... none of it even happened?
For some reason, I don't want to admit it to him.
So, you didn't like it? I tried...
I shrugged.
-Well... It wasn't that bad. After all, everyone has their own tastes, and...
-Yeah...
Kir looked genuinely hurt. I immediately regretted saying anything about his music...
The world around us began to crumble into pieces and fade away. We found ourselves in a narrow corridor, with broken wires hanging from the ceiling.

I panicked, looking around, trying to figure out if I'd seen this place before. The air smelled of dampness and unease. Why does this place feel so familiar? It's like... I dreamt of it... And this bunker, it...
Feels like a place from my dreams.

-I know that if I open up to people, I'll get a slap in the face. And every time... Every damn time, I still try to be sincere, to share what's inside me, and... Whether it's my thoughts or my music...
-It's all useless. I'm doomed to wear a mask and hide...
If I don't want to be alone.
I felt uneasy. I needed to get out of here...
-Sorry, I...
-Why do I want to be around people so badly if society is always against me?
-I don't understand myself...
-I don't understand...
-I don't understand.
-Can I... Can I go?
Kir stood off to the side, seemingly struggling to hold back tears.
Damn. Acting like a girl.
-Mira, I... I need to be alone. You don't need to see me... like this.
He snapped his fingers, and darkness enveloped my vision.
What?
I felt around the space. Good, there's a floor here... That's something.
I felt the metallic sphere on my head.
Am I home?
I reached out and removed the helmet.
The minute hand was just a couple of minutes past where it was when I'd entered the Net.
Maybe... it was all a dream?
Like... lucid dreams. Where you can do whatever you want.
But I still have the helmet... So, it wasn't all just a dream. Or it was... not quite a dream.
I wonder... would anyone believe me... That I was there, in the Net, and... And I could actually feel it, I could practically touch it.
If someone told me something like that... I'd never believe it.
-Hey! Where have you been?
-Oh, it's you again!
-By the way, I pooped on the floor. Clean it up.
-Oh god...
Looks like the day is almost over... Hard to believe!
I'm so tired...
A little more, and I'll melt into a puddle.
More and more, I'm convinced that everything happening to me isn't random.
It's like someone decided I should have a purpose. A purpose known only to them...
And this person controls me and my life however they want.
I don't know if I like it or not...
On one hand - I don't have to make any decisions.
On the other...
Who knows where this will lead me.
A knock on the door...
Huh?
Someone's here?
I'm not expecting anyone. Who could it be?
On tiptoes, I crept to the front door. Another knock echoed. Through the peephole, I immediately saw a cap sloppily pulled down over an ugly face. It's Tolik...

Another round of banging on the door. This time louder. What does he want... His lifeless, maniacal stare wasn't aimed at the door but straight through it, as if he was looking directly at me. Could he be here because of the body in the bathroom? Not this...
I decided to open up. I'd probably regret it later... Hesitating, I slid the bolt to the side. Without waiting for an invitation, Tolik pulled the door handle and stepped inside the apartment.
-Why didn't you open up? I was just passing by and thought I'd drop in.
Of course, I didn't believe that at all.
-They... found a body. In the 'Fox Trap.' Maybe... you know something about it?
Something clenched unpleasantly in my lower abdomen.
-No... Absolutely nothing.
I tried not to look him in the eye. Son of a bitch, why is he staring like that?
-And... you don't want to tell me anything? Maybe someone's bothering you?
That tone would make anyone crack. But not me. A cold sweat broke out on my forehead.
-No, absolutely nothing. I'm... I'm fine. Really.
-Well... All right.
-Enjoyed yourselves, did you?
-You... Mean with Alya?
I coughed, struggling to speak right away. My voice was trembling for some reason.
Tolik stayed silent in response.
-Good... It's nice for her to get out sometimes. Anyway, see you. Be careful.
-Maybe some tea?
Tolik chuckled and left, slamming the door behind him.
-Brr... Get lost already, fucker...
-"Fox Trap"
-He definitely noticed I was hiding something. He'll definitely start suspecting me... I'm in deep trouble. Should I run away, maybe... I don't know what to do!
I need fresh air.
My butt slowly hit the floor, sliding down near the door. I can't make a sound...
Tolik kept knocking persistently. Knock-knock-knock. I'm not home.
After a prolonged knocking, the door handle nervously jiggled up and down as if it was about to jump out along with the lock mechanism. Why is he trying to open the door when he can see it's locked?
Now he's added kicking the door to the handle's rattling.
... The lock will break and fall out, and he'll enter my apartment!
Leave... Please...
I'm begging you, go away.
I can't stand this noise anymore. Go away, go away, go away!
I can't. I can't!
Why won't he leave? Why?
-Mira! I know you're in there, open up!
-Mira, open up, it's Uncle Tolik.
-Are you deaf? Open the door.
Suddenly everything went silent. The knocking stopped, and a thick silence settled around me again.
-You buried your dad, don't be mean to me at least...
My jaw clenched so hard my teeth began to hurt. If I had even a little less patience, I would have flung the door open and slapped Tolik right across the face.
-Fine, fine. If Alina is with you, take care of her, please. I'll go.
Despite his words, Tolik didn't hurry to leave, still shuffling near the door and muttering some incoherent nonsense under his breath.
Finally, I heard his footsteps echoing against the old tile floor outside.
Why does he care where Alina goes...
Maybe he came because of the incident at 'Fox Trap'? He'll definitely start suspecting me... I'm in deep trouble. Should I run away, maybe... I don't know what to do! I need fresh air.
As soon as the footsteps outside faded, I darted out.
The spicy, cold air further irritated my brain... What's going to happen to me? I have no hope for anything good.

I looked around my courtyard. It was asleep, apparently in real 'nighttime.' I'd lost track of time long ago... Despite that, the world keeps on living, unaware of me. Is that bad? And does it need to notice me at all? Who am I to matter to it? I just live my life, separate...
A night bird began to sing nervously from a tree.
The bushes rustled, and a person leapt out at me. I barely saw that he held some curved stick in his hand.
-Get down!
He knocked me down, and we fell to the cold ground.
-What the hell?!
The guy opened his mouth as if screaming at the top of his lungs, and covered his ears with his hands.
The bird, startled, fluttered away.
-Eh...doko desu ka?
-Huh?
-Is he talking to me?
-Nihonjin?
-Niho... What? What do you want?
-I need to get to the center, the station, you understand? I have orders...
-You're holding a stick instead of a gun. Are you playing war games?
-Huh?
He looked at his 'weapon' and threw it to the ground.
-Who are you?
I pushed him away and ran back to my apartment.
-I... I'll find you, I'll come back!
No way! I'm not going back out there. No one's going to make me.
-Enough of this!
The heavy door closed, and I slumped against the wall. Exhausted by the madness surrounding me, I fell asleep in seconds.
